tools.name: start_order
tools.description: Start an order for the shopper on this storefront. Give the shopper's email address (ask them first; they get one confirmation email) or a connection key they made on their account. The answer holds the order reference (mo1_…): keep it and send it with every later call as Authorization: Bearer mo1_…

tools.name: status
tools.description: The state of the order reference (pending until the shopper confirms the email, active, paying, placed), whether the email is confirmed, the cart lines and totals, what the checkout still needs, and the next step to take. Use it to resume an order and after the shopper says they confirmed the email.

tools.name: view_checkout
tools.description: What the order still needs before it can be placed: lines, totals in the storefront currency, the address snapshot or the shopper's saved addresses, shipping methods with prices, the payment methods this order may use, and next. tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Place the order and start its payment. First confirm the order, its total and the terms of sale (/pg/terms.html on the store) with the shopper; send accept_terms true only after their explicit yes. With a confirmed email (path A) the order is placed at once and the answer gives the payment step: pay

tools.name: check_payment
tools.description: The payment state of the order (unpaid, pending, paid), its last attempt and the next step. After a failed or cancelled payment the cart is open again and place_order starts a new attempt. Needs the order reference from start_order (Authorization: Bearer mo1_… or the ref argument).

tools.name: cancel_payment
tools.description: Stops the open payment attempt of the order, for example a bank or card page the shopper closed or wants to replace, so the cart opens again and place_order can start another method (bank transfer once the email is confirmed). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.afhaalgroothandel.be" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, shipping_costs, product_details, start_order, view_checkout, place_order, cancel_payment, order_history · Private data: store_info · Public sink: edit_cart, start_order, status, view_checkout, set_checkout, place_order, cancel_payment, order_history · Destructive: edit_cart, set_checkout.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, shipping_costs, product_details, start_order, view_checkout, place_order, cancel_payment, order_history · Private data: store_info · Public sink: edit_cart, start_order, status, view_checkout, set_checkout, place_order, cancel_payment, order_history · Destructive: edit_cart, set_checkout

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
